context.why: This feature is built, reviewed and open for the maintainer's review. After reading the running API he agreed three further changes, recorded in specs/011-restful-api/decisions.md D26 and as tasks T071 to T073 in tasks.md Phase 10. The specification is already changed to match (User Story 5 narrative and scenarios 5 to 7, FR-036, FR-037, FR-045). Make exactly these three changes.
prior_decisions: decisions.md D26 is the whole instruction; read it, and D25 before it.

T071: delete SampleDiscoveryView, MeasurementDiscoveryView and their shared base and entry serializer from fairdm/api/viewsets.py (and serializers.py if the entry serializer lives there), their two paths from fairdm/api/urls.py, and the two catalogue links FairDMAPIRouter.get_api_root_view adds in fairdm/api/router.py; if the router subclass then does nothing a plain DefaultRouter does not, keep the public name `fairdm_api_router` and simplify the class away or leave it empty of overrides, whichever is less code. Delete the tests that cover the catalogues (tests/test_api/test_router.py TestCatalogues, TestCatalogueCounts, the catalogue parts of TestRoot, the older TestSampleDiscoveryEndpoint, TestMeasurementDiscoveryEndpoint and TestAPIRootContainsDiscoveryLinks if still present; the catalogue response test in tests/test_api/test_schema.py; demo/tests/test_api_smoke.py's catalogue tests; the unpublished-dataset test's catalogue-count case in tests/test_api/test_filters.py) and name each in progress.md. These deletions are authorised. GET /api/v1/samples/ and /api/v1/measurements/ must then answer 404, and the root must link to every list route and nothing else. Grep the whole repository for `discovery`, `catalogue`, `catalog`, `sample-types` and `measurement-types` afterwards, including docs/, fairdm/api/settings.py (FAIRDM_API_DESCRIPTION mentions the discovery endpoints), docstrings and CHANGELOG.md, and remove or correct every mention.

T072: every list accepts `modified_after` and `modified_before`, each an ISO 8601 date or date-time, matching the record's `modified` field (greater-than-or-equal and less-than-or-equal). Projects and datasets have no filter set in the API today and contributors neither; the registered types get theirs through FairDMFilterBackend (fairdm/api/filters.py), which builds the API's own subclass of the type's filter set. Add the two filters in ONE place that every list goes through, so no list can be without them, without changing the filter sets the portal's own pages use. A value that cannot be read as a moment is answered 400 naming the parameter. Both parameters must appear for every list in the generated schema (the schema tests from story 5 compare what the schema lists with what the API acts on). Contributors have `modified` too; check each model really has the field before relying on it. Add an index decision note only if `modified` is not already indexed: check the model field and say what you found in the report, do not add a migration.

T073: today every sample type's operations carry the one tag `samples` and every measurement type's `measurements`, the schema has no top-level `tags`, a type's display name appears nowhere, and each type's component schema takes its `description` from the docstring of BaseSampleSerializer or BaseMeasurementSerializer, which is written for the framework's developers. Change the schema generation, in fairdm/api/schema.py and where generate_viewset sets things up, so that: (a) each registered type's operations are tagged with the type's own plural name (str(model._meta.verbose_name_plural), as the registration gives it); (b) the schema's top-level `tags` list has one entry per registered type with that name and a description built from the registration: config.description if set, else config.metadata.description (see how generate_viewset already picks the operation description, and keep one function that both use), followed, where the registration gives them, by the authority (name, short name, website), the citation (text and DOI), the keywords, and with `externalDocs` set to the repository_url; never metadata.maintainer or metadata.maintainer_email; (c) each type's component schema (and its Patched and Paginated variants where drf-spectacular gives them a description) carries the type's own description and a `title` of the type's verbose_name, not the base class docstring; (d) projects, datasets and contributors get a top-level tag entry too, with the description their viewsets already have, so every tag used by an operation is described; (e) no description anywhere in the generated schema contains text from a docstring of the framework's base serializer or viewset classes (a test should look for a distinctive phrase such as 'Base DRF serializer' and ':class:'). Use drf-spectacular's own mechanisms (extend_schema / extend_schema_view tags on the generated viewset, extend_schema_serializer or a postprocessing hook for component descriptions, the existing postprocessing hook for top-level tags), whichever is least code. ModelMetadata, Authority and Citation are in fairdm/registry/config.py; demo/config.py has registrations that use all of them. Lazy translation strings must be turned into text when the schema is built. Tests assert on structure and on values taken from the registration, never on wording of our own.
Existing tests in tests/test_api/test_settings.py (TestSchemaComponentNaming, TestEndpointDescriptions) pin parts of the old schema shape: update the ones this changes and name them in progress.md.

Documentation: docs/portal-development/restful-api.md has sections on the discovery catalogue (remove), on model descriptions in the API docs (rewrite to say which registration metadata appears where), and on filtering (add the two changed-since parameters and how a harvester uses them: remember when you last read, ask for what changed after it). The page for people using a portal gains the same short note on reading only what is new. Update this feature's entry in CHANGELOG.md: the catalogue endpoints are removed (replace the line added for D25 about what an entry holds), the two new parameters, and the documentation's sections per type.
Update feature-state.json for T071, T072 and T073 (status, attempts, evidence with tests, commands, code as path:line, verified_by_ci) and tick them in tasks.md.
Write your completion report to specs/011-restful-api/report-fix-3.json. Do not run `ruff check` with fixing over the whole tree: it rewrites unrelated test files. Lint only the files you touch.

acceptance.given_when_then: Given the API, then the two catalogue addresses answer 404, the root links to every list and nothing else, and no code, test or page mentions the catalogues.

Given every list, then modified_after and modified_before narrow it to records changed after and before the moment given, an unreadable moment is a 400, and both are among the list's parameters in the schema.

Given the generated schema, then each registered type has its own section named with its plural name and described from its registration, with authority, citation, keywords and repository link where given and never a maintainer's details, and no description is a base class docstring.
